Detected unusual patterns:

- Bear case shows 23.0% growth (unusual for a conservative scenario)
- Bull case shows 343.5% growth (extremely optimistic)

# ServiceNow Inc (NOW) Investment Analysis

## 1\. Executive Summary

ServiceNow Inc is a global provider of enterprise cloud computing software designed to manage, automate, and optimize digital workflows across complex corporate operations \[ [1](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-1), [2](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-2)\]. The company's proprietary Now Platform integrates legacy IT systems, departmental tools, and databases to serve as a unified system of action \[ [3](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-3)\]. This architecture orchestrates multi-departmental workflows, eliminating operational silos and maximizing process automation without requiring organizations to replace their underlying core databases or transactional applications \[ [1](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-1), [3](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-3)\].

ServiceNow’s monetization model is primarily subscription-based, with subscriptions accounting for approximately 97% of total revenues in fiscal year 2025 \[ [4](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-4)\]. The remaining 3% is generated through professional services, including consulting, customer implementation assistance, and training \[ [4](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-4)\]. Strategically, the subscription business operates on multi-year contract structures with high predictability, heavily backed by a historical renewal rate of 98% \[ [4](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-4), [5](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-5)\].

### Segment and Geographic Revenue Breakdown

The following table details ServiceNow's revenue distribution across segments, geographies, and high-value customer thresholds:

| Segment / Region / Customer Classification | Metrics & Distributions (FY2025) | Core Operational Significance |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Subscription Segment** | $12,883 Million (97.02% of total) \[ [6](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-6)\] | Represents the primary, highly predictable recurring revenue engine \[ [4](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-4)\]. |
| **Professional Services & Other** | $395 Million (2.98% of total) \[ [6](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-6)\] | Supports platform implementation, with a declining share over time as system integrators take over \[ [4](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-4)\]. |
| **North America Geography** | $8.35 Billion (62.87% of total) \[ [4](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-4), [7](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-7)\] | The dominant geographical segment, heavily anchored by mature enterprise markets in the United States \[ [4](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-4), [7](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-7)\]. |
| **EMEA Geography** | $3.40 Billion (25.60% of total) \[ [4](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-4), [7](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-7)\] | Key international market showing continuous, steady digital transformation demand \[ [4](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-4)\]. |
| **Asia-Pacific & Other** | $1.53 Billion (11.53% of total) \[ [4](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-4), [7](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-7)\] | The fastest-growing, highly underpenetrated geographic frontier \[ [4](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-4)\]. |
| **High-Value Enterprise Base** | 603 Customers with >$5M ACV \[ [6](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-6), [8](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-8)\] | Up from 502 in fiscal year 2024, demonstrating robust land-and-expand execution \[ [6](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-6), [8](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-8)\]. |

The core product suite consists of standard IT Service Management (ITSM), IT Operations Management (ITOM), HR Service Delivery, Customer Service Management (CSM), and Security, Risk, and Governance workflows \[ [1](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-1), [9](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-9)\]. These products serve massive global enterprises, federal governments, and critical infrastructure operators \[ [1](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-1), [10](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-10)\]. Organizations select ServiceNow over legacy alternatives due to the platform's ability to act as a single pane of glass, its modular and flexible low-code architecture, and its rapid deployment of generative artificial intelligence (AI) under the "Now Assist" and "AI Control Tower" architectures \[ [3](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-3), [9](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-9), [11](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-11)\].

## 2\. Business Drivers and Strategic Overview

The principal engine of ServiceNow’s financial expansion is its land-and-expand sales strategy \[ [9](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-9)\]. Typically, a customer enters the ecosystem through core ITSM tools to resolve internal IT helpdesk processes, subsequently adopting adjacent ITOM modules to map enterprise architecture \[ [9](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-9)\]. Over time, customers deploy non-IT solutions, such as HR Service Delivery, CSM, and strategic portfolio management tools \[ [9](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-9), [12](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-12)\]. This model creates compounding revenue expansion within the existing customer base, as evidenced by a 23% year-over-year growth in customers spending more than $5 million in annual contract value (ACV) as of the second quarter of fiscal year 2026 \[ [12](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-12)\].

### Competitive Advantages and Moat Analysis

ServiceNow possesses a wide economic moat rooted in high customer switching costs, ecosystem scale, and extensive distribution advantages \[ [1](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-1), [9](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-9)\]. Once the Now Platform is integrated into a customer's standard operating environment, it becomes the underlying orchestrator for internal employee services, external customer interactions, and real-time security alerts \[ [1](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-1), [3](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-3)\]. The integration requires significant capital, time, and training \[ [1](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-1)\]. Replacing ServiceNow introduces severe operational risk, custom-code disruption, and training costs \[ [1](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-1)\]. This is quantitatively demonstrated by the company's sustained 98% renewal rate \[ [4](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-4), [5](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-5)\].

With more than 75 billion workflows running on the platform annually, ServiceNow has reached an operational scale that smaller point-solution competitors cannot match \[ [3](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-3)\]. The platform acts as a workflow orchestration layer on top of ERP, CRM, and HCM systems of record, positioning ServiceNow as an essential operational layer that is difficult to bypass \[ [1](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-1), [3](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-3)\]. Furthermore, the company has built deep partnerships with primary technology providers, including joint integrations with NVIDIA (the Project Arc autonomous desktop agent and validated designs for the NVIDIA Enterprise AI Factory) \[ [12](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-12)\], Microsoft \[ [13](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-13)\], Lenovo \[ [12](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-12)\], and Anthropic, which acts as a design partner integrating the Claude large language model directly into ServiceNow's Action Fabric \[ [12](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-12)\].

### Total Addressable Market Opportunity

Management estimated the total addressable market (TAM) to be approximately $600 billion \[ [5](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-5)\]. This market size is supported by the platform's expansion from core IT management into adjacent, high-value enterprise software categories, including Customer Relationship Management (CRM), cybersecurity exposure management, and AI-native agentic workflows \[ [5](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-5), [10](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-10)\].

### Competitive Landscape and Position

The enterprise software landscape is highly competitive, yet ServiceNow occupies a unique space:

| Strategic Domain | Main Competitors | ServiceNow Strategic Position & Trend |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **IT Service Management (ITSM)** | Atlassian, Freshworks \[ [9](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-9), [14](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-14)\] | ServiceNow maintains a dominant market share in large enterprises \[ [1](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-1)\]. It continues to hold and gain ground, driven by its high-tier generative AI features \[ [9](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-9)\]. |
| **Customer Service Workflows (CSM)** | Salesforce \[ [2](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-2), [15](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-15)\] | ServiceNow is gaining market share by positioning its CSM tools not as basic customer databases, but as active workflow engines connecting front-office queries to back-office execution \[ [1](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-1), [9](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-9)\]. |
| **Cybersecurity Operations (SecOps)** | Palo Alto Networks, Fortinet, Microsoft, Claroty \[ [16](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-16)\] | ServiceNow is significantly expanding its position \[ [10](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-10)\]. The Security and Risk business crossed the $1 billion ACV threshold in the third quarter of fiscal year 2025 \[ [10](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-10), [17](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-17)\]. |

To accelerate its proactive cybersecurity and vulnerability remediation roadmap, ServiceNow announced a $7.75 billion cash acquisition of Armis Security, slated to close in the second half of fiscal year 2026 \[ [10](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-10), [18](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-18)\]. By integrating Armis’s real-time, agentless asset discovery and vulnerability exposure management (covering IT, OT, IoT, and medical devices) with ServiceNow's automated remediation workflows, the company expects to more than triple its market opportunity in the security and risk sector \[ [10](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-10), [17](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-17)\].

## 3\. Financial Performance and Valuation

### Latest Quarterly Financial Results (Q2 FY2026)

ServiceNow announced its financial results for the second quarter of fiscal year 2026 on July 22, 2026, for the period ended June 30, 2026 \[ [12](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-12), [13](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-13)\]. The company delivered strong top-line performance and raised its full-year guidance, though its GAAP earnings results faced pressure \[ [12](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-12), [19](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-19)\].

- **Total Revenue:** $3,987 million, representing a 24.0% year-over-year growth rate (22.5% in constant currency) \[ [12](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-12)\]. This surpassed the consensus analyst estimate of $3,927.42 million by 1.52% \[ [19](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-19)\].
- **Subscription Revenue:** $3,877 million, representing 24.5% year-over-year growth (23.0% in constant currency), beating the high end of the company's guidance range \[ [12](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-12)\].
- **Non-GAAP Operating Income:** $1,173 million, representing a non-GAAP operating margin of 29.5%, which beat management’s guidance \[ [13](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-13), [19](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-19)\].
- **Non-GAAP Adjusted EPS:** $0.90, beating the analyst consensus expectation of $0.86 by 5.05%, driven by operating leverage and cost efficiencies \[ [19](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-19), [20](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-20)\].
- **GAAP EPS:** $0.29, missing consensus analyst estimates of $0.32 by 9.17% \[ [19](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-19)\]. Sequentially, GAAP EPS fell 35.56% from the $0.45 posted in the first quarter of fiscal year 2026, primarily due to a lower GAAP operating margin of 4.1% and tax adjustments below the operating line \[ [19](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-19), [21](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-21)\].
- **Remaining Performance Obligations (RPO):** Total RPO stood at $29.0 billion (up 21.0% year-over-year) \[ [12](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-12)\]. Current RPO (cRPO)—revenue expected to be recognized over the next 12 months—stood at $13.20 billion (up 21.0% year-over-year, or 21.5% in constant currency) \[ [12](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-12)\].

| Q2 FY2026 Metric | Reported Result | Consensus Expectation | Performance Versus Expectations | YoY Growth Rate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Total Revenue** | $3,987M \[ [12](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-12)\] | $3,927M \[ [19](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-19)\] | Beat by 1.52% \[ [19](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-19)\] | 24.0% \[ [12](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-12)\] |
| **Subscription Revenue** | $3,877M \[ [12](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-12)\] | $3,820M \[ [22](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-22)\] | Beat by 1.49% | 24.5% \[ [12](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-12)\] |
| **Non-GAAP Operating Margin** | 29.50% \[ [13](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-13)\] | N/A | Beat Guidance | Slippage of 238 bps QoQ \[ [19](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-19)\] |
| **Non-GAAP Adjusted EPS** | $0.90 \[ [19](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-19)\] | $0.86 \[ [19](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-19)\] | Beat by 5.05% \[ [19](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-19)\] | 10.02% \[ [19](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-19)\] |
| **GAAP EPS** | $0.29 \[ [19](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-19)\] | $0.32 \[ [19](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-19)\] | Missed by 9.17% \[ [19](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-19)\] | Decline of 21.20% \[ [19](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-19)\] |
| **Current RPO (cRPO)** | $13.20B \[ [12](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-12)\] | N/A | Beat Guidance | 21.0% (21.5% CC) \[ [12](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-12)\] |

The GAAP EPS shortfall of $0.29 against non-GAAP results highlights the gap between adjusted and unadjusted performance in ServiceNow's financials \[ [19](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-19), [21](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-21)\]. GAAP operating margins were impacted by stock-based compensation (SBC), which accounted for 16% of total revenues, and amortization of acquired intangibles, which accounted for 5% of revenues \[ [11](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-11), [13](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-13)\]. Under the operating line, GAAP net income was also affected by a $51 million discrete tax benefit resulting from the release of a valuation allowance on deferred tax assets \[ [11](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-11), [13](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-13)\].

### Management Commentary and Guidance Adjustments

During the earnings call, Chief Financial Officer Gina Mastantuono highlighted the momentum of the AI portfolio, noting that the company’s AI offerings crossed $1 billion in ACV in the quarter \[ [19](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-19)\]. She also noted that the company is tracking ahead of its long-term target for AI to account for 30% of total ACV by 2030 \[ [19](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-19)\]. Chairman and CEO Bill McDermott highlighted that agentic AI deployments increased ninefold over a nine-month period, establishing the platform as an "AI control tower" \[ [12](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-12), [13](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-13)\].

Following these results, management adjusted its outlook:

\\* **FY2026 Subscription Revenue Guidance:** Raised the midpoint of full-year subscription revenue guidance to $15.77 billion (representing 21% constant-currency growth) \[ [19](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-19), [23](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-23)\]. The revised guidance range of $15.76 billion to $15.78 billion is up from the previous projection of $15.74 billion to $15.78 billion \[ [20](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-20), [23](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-23)\].

\\* **FY2026 Operating Margin Guidance:** Raised the full-year non-GAAP operating margin outlook to 31.5% \[ [19](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-19), [23](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-23)\].

\\* **FY2026 Free Cash Flow Margin Guidance:** Reaffirmed at 35.0% \[ [23](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-23)\].

\\* **Dilution and Share Count Management:** Announced an additional $5.0 billion share repurchase authorization to manage dilution, with plans for an immediate $2.0 billion accelerated share repurchase (ASR) program \[ [6](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-6)\].

### Market and Stock Price Impact

Following the announcement on July 22, 2026, ServiceNow’s stock price rose approximately 4% to 5% in post-market and next-day trading, reflecting positive investor sentiment regarding the subscription revenue beat and raised guidance \[ [20](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-20), [22](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-22)\]. However, the stock experienced volatility through late August and September 2026 \[ [24](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-24)\]. Concerns over competitive announcements from OpenAI, macro rotation out of high-multiple growth software, and rising interest rates exerted downward pressure on ServiceNow, bringing the share price to $140.85 as of mid-September 2026 \[ [24](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-24), [25](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-25)\]. Analyst sentiment remains positive, with more than 90% of sell-side analysts maintaining a Buy-equivalent rating, supported by price target upgrades from BMO Capital ($150) and Needham ($155) \[ [20](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-20), [24](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-24)\].

### Underlying Drivers and Financial Valuation Model

To evaluate ServiceNow's enterprise value, investors must look past GAAP metrics, which are impacted by stock-based compensation (averaging 16% of total revenue) and amortization of acquired intangibles from transactions such as Moveworks, Veza, and Armis \[ [11](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-11), [26](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-26)\]. The primary valuation driver is the company's strong free cash flow (FCF) generation \[ [21](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-21)\]. In fiscal year 2025, the company generated $4.64 billion in FCF on a 35% margin \[ [6](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-6)\]. The business operates efficiently under the Rule of 56 (21% subscription constant-currency revenue growth + 35% FCF margin) and is targeting a Rule of 60+ by 2030 (combining constant-currency growth and FCF margin above 60%) \[ [13](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-13), [27](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-27)\].

The normalized trailing Price-to-Earnings (P/E) ratio is 82.83x (with a trailing GAAP P/E of 88.90x), which represents a premium relative to peers like Salesforce (P/E of 22.52x) \[ [14](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-14), [28](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-28)\]. This valuation is supported by:

1\. A consistent 23.1% 5-year revenue compound annual growth rate (CAGR) \[ [21](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-21)\].

2\. High revenue visibility from a $29.0 billion RPO back-log \[ [12](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-12)\].

3\. Prepayments from enterprise customers, which help finance operations without relying on dilutive equity issuances or external debt \[ [4](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-4)\].

## 4\. Risk Assessment and Macroeconomic Considerations

### Execution Risks

ServiceNow is executing its largest-ever acquisition strategy, led by the pending $7.75 billion cash purchase of Armis Security \[ [10](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-10), [18](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-18)\] and the $2.85 billion acquisition of Moveworks \[ [18](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-18)\]. Historically, ServiceNow has favored native product development over large acquisitions, which has allowed it to maintain a single codebase \[ [29](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-29)\]. Integrating non-native architectures into the Now Platform introduces technical complexity, data model refactoring risks, and potential friction for customers \[ [29](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-29)\]. If these integrations stall, subscription gross margins could face pressure \[ [15](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-15)\].

### Competitive Risks

While ServiceNow dominates the ITSM sector, its growth targets require expanding into the highly competitive cybersecurity and CRM markets \[ [5](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-5), [16](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-16)\]. In CRM, it faces Salesforce’s established market position \[ [15](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-15)\]. In security, it competes with platform security vendors like Palo Alto Networks, Fortinet, and Microsoft \[ [16](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-16)\]. Additionally, there is a risk that rapid advancements in foundational large language models (such as OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra) could allow enterprise clients to build custom autonomous workflows natively, bypassing third-party orchestration layers like ServiceNow \[ [24](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-24)\].

### Capital Allocation and Balance Sheet Risks

To fund the $7.75 billion Armis acquisition, ServiceNow plans to use a combination of cash on hand and new debt \[ [10](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-10)\]. The company's cash and cash equivalents fell to $2.50 billion as of June 30, 2026, while its total debt rose to $8.45 billion \[ [21](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-21), [30](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-30)\]. This represents a shift from its net cash position in fiscal year 2025, where total debt was $2.40 billion against $10.1 billion in total cash and investments \[ [30](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-30), [31](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-31)\]. Although cash flow from operations remains strong, the higher debt load reduces capital allocation flexibility for stock repurchases and additional M&A \[ [21](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-21)\].

### Macroeconomic Sensitivities

As a high-multiple technology stock, ServiceNow is sensitive to changes in interest rates and macroeconomic cycles \[ [24](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-24)\]. In periods of rising interest rates, valuation multiples for growth stocks typically contract \[ [24](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-24)\]. Furthermore, if global macroeconomic headwinds lead to corporate IT budget cuts, enterprise clients may delay upgrading to premium tier subscriptions (such as Now Assist), slowing growth in new annual contract value \[ [24](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-24)\].

### Risk Framework and Key Indicators

To help investors monitor these risks, the analytical framework below outlines potential issues, early warning signs, and factors that could affect the long-term investment thesis:

- **What Could Go Wrong:** Technical integration challenges with the Armis platform could lead to customer friction and delayed product rollouts, slowing new sales momentum in the Security and Risk segment \[ [15](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-15), [29](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-29)\].
- **Early Warning Signs:** A deceleration in current RPO (cRPO) growth below 18% \[ [12](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-12)\], a leveling off in transactions exceeding $5 million in ACV \[ [12](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-12)\], or a contraction in the subscription gross margin below 78% on a non-GAAP basis \[ [13](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-13)\].
- **Long-Term Thesis Damage:** A drop in the company's core subscription renewal rate below 95% (historically at 98%), which would signal a decline in customer switching costs or a shift toward alternative workflow platforms \[ [4](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-4), [5](https://flash.stocksentinel.ai/research/NOW#ref-5)\].

# ServiceNow Inc. (NYSE: NOW) — Deep Analysis Report

### NOW is down 55% from peak while cRPO is growing 22.5% — that gap is either the opportunity or the warning, depending on one number you can't get from the filings.

[![Jin's avatar](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!nfGY!,w_36,h_36,c_fill,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F4de70d72-bd66-4655-a718-f212e7073106_1024x1024.png)](https://substack.com/@jinlow)

[Jin](https://substack.com/@jinlow)

May 11, 2026

2

1

Share

**Data retrieved:** May 12, 2026

**Primary sources:** ServiceNow FY2025 earnings press release (Jan 28, 2026), Q1 2026 earnings release (Apr 23, 2026), CNBC, MacroTrends, GuruFocus, FinanceCharts, Morningstar, Yahoo Finance, StockAnalysis, Pulse2, SimplyWallSt.

**Analytical status:** Resolves with Q2 2026 earnings (expected late July 2026).

* * *

#### **1\. Company Snapshot**

ServiceNow is an enterprise cloud software platform that automates and manages digital workflows across IT, HR, customer service, security operations, and increasingly finance and supply chain. It is headquartered in Santa Clara, California, and listed on the NYSE.

**Software Category Classification:** Category One — Enterprise Workflow Platform. This is a horizontal platform with deep workflow-process embedding, not a point-solution application. The platform _is_ the workflow layer across the enterprise stack — not a feature within it. The closest analogue in the evaluation framework is the “Platform” subcategory.

**Stock Price (as of May 8, 2026):** ~$91.60 per share (post 5-for-1 split adjusted) — **Market Cap: ~$94B**

⚠️ **Most material context entering valuation:** ServiceNow’s market cap has declined approximately 51.6% year-over-year from its 2025 peak of ~$190B+, while underlying business fundamentals (20–22% revenue growth, 35% FCF margin, cRPO at 22–25%) have remained broadly intact. This fundamental price divergence is the central analytical tension of this report.

[![ServiceNow | LinkedIn](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!oc-w!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fc3521adb-25f9-4caa-b4b0-64e9a7707464_1200x627.jpeg)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!oc-w!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2Fc3521adb-25f9-4caa-b4b0-64e9a7707464_1200x627.jpeg) https://www.linkedin.com/company/servicenow

* * *

#### **2\. Business Model Analysis**

#### **2.1 Products & Services**

ServiceNow’s core offering is the **Now Platform** — a unified cloud-based system of record for enterprise workflows. Primary product families: IT Service Management (ITSM), IT Operations Management (ITOM), HR Service Delivery, Customer Service Management (CSM), Security Operations, and Strategic Portfolio Management.

Recent additions: **Now Assist** (generative AI layer), **Workflow Data Fabric** (data orchestration), and **RaptorDB** (proprietary high-performance database engine).

**Acquisition status as of May 2026:**

- **Moveworks** (agentic AI for employee support): Closed December 15, 2025

- **Armis** (OT/IoT cybersecurity asset visibility, $7.75B): Closed April 2026 — ahead of original second-half 2026 timeline. Now fully consolidated. Armis adds ~125bps to FY2026 subscription revenue growth guidance, but introduces 75bps operating margin drag and 200bps FCF margin drag

- **Veza** (identity security governance): **Not yet closed** as of May 2026. Deal size undisclosed. This is the third concurrent integration in flight — a non-trivial execution risk


⚠️ **Three simultaneous major integrations** (Moveworks, Armis, Veza) create execution risk beyond their individual financial impacts: management bandwidth is finite, platform architecture coherence is harder to maintain across three new product lines concurrently, and go-to-market motion complexity rises. This is the “integration distraction” risk for serial acquirers and deserves explicit weight in the risk framework.

Subscribe

#### **2.2 Revenue Model**

ServiceNow is overwhelmingly subscription software. Subscription revenues represented **$12,883M of total FY2025 revenues of $13,278M — approximately 97% subscription**. Professional services are intentionally sub-scale; implementation work is routed to certified partners (Accenture, Deloitte, KPMG, Wipro).

**Critical pricing-model transition in progress:** The base model is seat/user licensed. ServiceNow is mid-transition to consumption/outcome-based pricing via Now Assist AI SKUs. As of Q1 2026, AI features are being **bundled into every product and package rather than sold as a discrete SKU overlay**. The CEO explicitly confirmed this in the Q1 2026 earnings call. Near-term effect: ACV expansion on renewals. Medium-term effect: loss of disaggregated visibility into AI-specific ACV, which makes the additive vs. cannibalization question structurally harder to answer from external data. See Section 5.4 for full treatment.

#### **2.3 Target Customers**

ServiceNow serves large enterprises and government entities. As of Q4 2025:

- **603 customers** with >$5M ACV, representing ~20% YoY growth

- **244 transactions** over $1M net new ACV in Q4 2025 alone

- **2,109 customers** with >$1M ACV as of Q4 2024, growing 12% YoY


The customer profile is systematically upper-enterprise. Sub-enterprise deployment is a structural gap in go-to-market, and the primary arena where Microsoft’s bundled competitive motion is most dangerous (see Sections 4.3 and 5.4).

#### **2.4 Upstream & Downstream Relationships**

**Upstream:** ServiceNow runs on hyperscalers (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud). No data center ownership; modest CapEx. Multi-cloud strategy limits single-provider lock-in. Hyperscaler concentration remains the primary supplier risk but is structurally managed.

**Downstream:** Multi-year, deeply embedded enterprise contracts with upfront billings. Accounts receivable are predictable. Customer switching costs are the dominant feature of downstream relationships — discussed fully in Section 6.2.

* * *

#### **3\. Financial Statement Analysis**

#### **3.1 Profitability**

[![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!iFmG!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F8da14d46-12ae-406d-b692-1d65fb34a169_726x270.png)](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!iFmG!,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F8da14d46-12ae-406d-b692-1d65fb34a169_726x270.png)

_Sources: MacroTrends, ServiceNow Q4 FY2025 earnings release, Q1 2026 earnings release. FY2022 GAAP net income per analyst data. FY2024 GAAP net income requires a 10-K verification before investment._

✅ **Confirmed:** FY2025 blended gross margin 77.5%; subscription gross margin ~80% GAAP, ~83% non-GAAP. FY2025 FCF $4.636B at 35% FCF margin. FCF margin materially exceeds the 20% framework threshold for mature software.

✅ **Confirmed Q1 2026:** Total revenue $3.77B (+22% nominal); subscription revenue $3,671M (+22% nominal, **+19% constant currency**). GAAP net income $469M. The nominal/constant-currency gap of ~300bps is a persistent structural feature of the business, not a transient artifact.

⚠️ **GAAP vs. Non-GAAP divergence — structural flag:**

- FY2025 GAAP operating income: $1.824B (13.5% margin)

- FY2025 non-GAAP operating income: $4.149B (31% margin)

- **Gap: $2.3B — approximately 125% of GAAP operating income**


This gap is overwhelmingly stock-based compensation (SBC) and acquisition-related costs. SBC as a percentage of revenue ran at approximately 17.3% in FY2025 ($2.3B on $13.3B revenue). This is structural, not incidental. Management’s “Rule of 55+” metric is a non-GAAP construct. The correct GAAP P/E anchor is ~50–52x TTM (see Section 7.2), not any non-GAAP derivative. SBC is a real economic cost — investors ignoring it are ignoring annual dilution.

⚠️ **ROE of ~15%:** At the minimum threshold but not exceptional. ROE is structurally depressed by SBC (diluting equity via share grants) and goodwill accumulation from acquisitions (inflating the equity denominator). Armis + Moveworks + Veza will push this lower for the foreseeable future. **The appropriate primary metric for ServiceNow is ROIC ex-goodwill/intangibles**, not reported ROE. Reported ROE understates true capital efficiency on tangible assets.

⚠️ **FCF margin forward guidance:** FY2026 FCF margin is guided at **35%** — flat vs. FY2025 but inclusive of Armis integration drag (~200bps headwind). Base-case FCF margin normalization post-integration is **34–35%**, not the 36%+ that a simple linear extrapolation of pre-acquisition trends would suggest. The 36%+ outcome requires either (a) management to reduce SBC as a % of revenue explicitly, or (b) AI infrastructure capex to deliver measurable gross margin leverage by FY2028. Neither is assumed in the base case.

#### **3.2 Software-Specific Metrics (RPO / cRPO / NRR)**

![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!eGJJ!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F7d863f96-f1f9-4b75-ae52-596fcf303d1c_735x159.png)

**cRPO base (Q1 2026):** $10.47B growing 22.5% YoY (primary source: Q1 2026 earnings release). This is a deceleration from Q4 2025’s 25% — the first crack in the “accelerating booked growth” narrative. The three-quarter sequential movement (19% → 25% → 22.5%) is not noise; it warrants explicit tracking.

**cRPO / TTM subscription revenue ratio:** $10.47B / $13.56B TTM subscription revenue = **0.77x** (TTM = $12,883M FY2025 + $3,671M Q1 2026 − ~$2,995M Q1 2025 ≈ $13,559M). A declining ratio over sequential quarters signals contract duration compression or renewal pricing pressure; stability signals neither. Current 0.77x is approximately stable vs. prior periods.

**cRPO–revenue conversion gap:** cRPO growing at 22.5% while constant-currency subscription revenue grows at 19% implies a ~350bps lag. This is partially explained by FX timing differences in revenue recognition. A sustained and widening gap would indicate either deteriorating conversion rates or contract structure changes. This ratio should be modeled explicitly in forward revenue forecasts.

**RPO stability:** Total RPO of $30.3B growing 26.8% YoY in Q1 2026, stable from Q4 2025’s 26.5%. The narrow cRPO/RPO growth differential (22.5% vs. 26.8%) indicates moderate contract lengthening but not at alarming levels. No evidence of excessive duration extension masking near-term weakness.

**On NRR:** ServiceNow does not formally disclose NRR in earnings releases. Third-party analyst estimates place NRR consistently above 120–125%. ⚠️ This figure is not primary-source verified. It cannot be confirmed to the exact number without a formal SEC disclosure. The cRPO trajectory is consistent with strong net expansion but does not substitute for a direct NRR figure.

**Q1 2026 re-acceleration note (corrected):** The nominal subscription growth of 22% (Q1 2026) versus 21% (Q4 2025) is a modest positive. **On a constant-currency basis, Q1 2026 at 19% represents a deceleration, not acceleration.** The “re-acceleration signal” from the original report does not hold on the operationally cleaner constant-currency metric.

#### **3.3 Financial Health**

ServiceNow carried a D/E ratio of approximately 1.01 as of Q4 2025. Pre-Armis net cash position was approximately $800M ($5.8B cash vs. $5.0B long-term debt). Post-Armis close ($7.75B, substantially debt-financed), the balance sheet has likely swung to **net debt of approximately $5–6B**. This is the correct EV bridge adjustment — see Section 7.2. No going concern risks. The leverage increase is manageable given the FCF generation profile.

#### **3.4 Audit Opinion**

Auditor: PricewaterhouseCoopers. FY2024 10-K audit opinion: unqualified. ⚠️ FY2025 10-K audit opinion has not been retrieved directly for this analysis — verification from the SEC filing is required before investment. No material weaknesses have been publicly reported.

#### **4\. Competitive Position (Porter’s Five Forces)**

#### **4.1 Threat of New Entrants — Low**

Enterprise workflow automation requires compliance certifications (FedRAMP, SOC2, HIPAA, ISO), a global professional services ecosystem, and two decades of ITSM workflow data and process template libraries. Platform-level displacement by new entrants is structurally difficult. Point-solution startups (ticketing, approvals) exist but cannot replicate the Now Platform’s workflow depth and integration breadth at enterprise scale.

#### **4.2 Competitive Rivalry — Moderate in Core; High in Adjacencies**

In core ITSM, ServiceNow holds near-oligopoly status. The distant second tier — BMC Helix, Atlassian Jira Service Management — does not threaten the installed base. The genuine rivalry is in expansion adjacencies: CRM (Salesforce), HR workflows (Workday, SAP), and security operations (Palo Alto, CrowdStrike). In these adjacencies, ServiceNow is the challenger, not the incumbent, and the single-platform consolidation argument, while real, is harder to prove in greenfield deals where the incumbent is deeply embedded.

#### **4.3 Threat of Substitutes — Moderate, Rising; Microsoft Is the Specific Proximate Risk**

The generic AI agent substitute threat (Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini) is real, but generic framing understates the specific mechanism. Microsoft’s threat is not that Copilot is technically superior to ServiceNow’s ITSM workflow engine — it almost certainly is not for complex multi-workflow scenarios. The threat is that Microsoft can offer **“good enough bundled”** IT workflow automation as part of Microsoft 365 / Azure agreements that enterprises already pay for. This is the most historically dangerous competitive motion against best-of-breed SaaS.

Microsoft’s leverage is most potent in the sub-$1M ACV new logo segment — ServiceNow’s structural market gap (Section 2.3). Microsoft already owns the identity layer (Azure Active Directory), the productivity layer (Microsoft 365), and increasingly the AI orchestration layer (Azure AI Foundry). ServiceNow’s counter-positioning — “the AI orchestration layer above Microsoft” — is coherent but requires Microsoft to accept a subordinate role that is commercially against its own interest.

**Moat qualification by segment:**

- **$5M+ ACV installed base:** Moat is Wide — multi-workflow complexity, years of embedded configurations, organizational process dependency, and partner ecosystem investment make displacement extraordinarily expensive

- **Sub-$1M ACV new logo acquisition:** Moat extension is contested — Microsoft bundling is most dangerous here, and this is where TAM realization risk is concentrated


⚠️ The causal variable for moat strength is **module depth and multi-workflow attach rate**, not ACV bin. A $2M ACV customer running ITSM+ITOM+HR+Security is more entrenched than a single-module $6M ACV customer. ACV is a proxy for complexity; the underlying driver is workflow breadth. If ServiceNow ever discloses module attach rates for new logos, that becomes the superior moat monitoring metric.

ServiceNow’s strategic response (Now Assist, AI Agent Orchestrator, Moveworks) is to position the platform as the orchestration substrate _for_ AI agents rather than the UI layer being replaced _by_ them. This is the correct strategic framing. Execution risk is real and unresolved.

#### **4.4 Bargaining Power of Suppliers — Moderate**

Hyperscaler concentration (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud) is the primary risk. Multi-cloud strategy limits single-provider leverage. Geographic concentration in US-hosted infrastructure creates compliance complexity for regulated international customers.

#### **4.5 Bargaining Power of Buyers — Low (ServiceNow’s Favor)**

Deeply embedded, multi-year contracts with workflow logic, custom configurations, and employee training invested in the platform make displacement extraordinarily expensive. The platform grows stickier as module count increases. Pricing power and consistent contract expansion are direct consequences. Buyers have no credible at-scale alternative.

#### **5\. Macro & Industry Environment**

#### **5.1 Federal Government Exposure**

US Federal government enterprise software spending has been a headwind. DOGE-driven efficiency initiatives create simultaneous risk (budget cuts reducing seat counts) and opportunity (workflow modernization mandates driving new deployments). Federal is a meaningful revenue segment — this dynamic warrants tracking across H2 2026 earnings commentary.

#### **5.2 Regulatory & Antitrust Dynamics**

No material antitrust scrutiny of ServiceNow specifically. Armis acquisition regulatory review, if any, did not prevent the April 2026 close. ServiceNow is not in the regulatory crosshairs facing Google, Meta, or Microsoft.

#### **5.3 Macro & International Factors**

FX headwinds are structural, not transient. Q4 2025 cRPO grew 25% USD but 21% constant currency (~400bps drag). Q1 2026 subscription revenue grew 22% nominal but 19% constant currency (~300bps drag). International expansion (EMEA, APAC) is a growth vector but also a perpetual FX exposure. All growth metrics should be evaluated on a constant-currency basis as the primary operational signal.

#### **5.4 AI Impact Assessment — Dual: Tailwind (Near-Term) + Structural Risk (Medium-Term)**

**Near-term tailwind (confirmed):** Now Assist net new ACV more than doubled YoY in Q4 2025. Now Assist annual ACV target raised from $1B to **$1.5B** in Q1 2026 earnings — a 50% upward revision to internal forecast. AI upsell within existing accounts is real and measurable.

**Bundling change (Q1 2026 — new information):** The CEO confirmed AI is now “built into every product and package — not a separate purchase.” This is a strategic pivot. Near-term effect: ACV expansion on renewals as AI becomes table stakes. Medium-term effect: **loss of disaggregated visibility into AI-specific ACV**. If AI is embedded in every SKU, external observers cannot distinguish additive AI ACV from repriced seat ACV. The bundling move likely boosts total ACV; it also makes the additive/cannibalization question structurally harder to answer from public filings going forward.

**Structural risk (medium-term — inference, not settled):** If AI agents autonomously handle workflows previously requiring human user interactions, seat count justification erodes without the agentic orchestration layer capturing compensating revenue. The central unresolved question is whether ServiceNow successfully transitions from a seat-count-justified platform to an AI orchestration substrate. This is not resolvable with currently available data. It requires 2–3 more quarters of blended ACV and constant-currency growth trends.

**Professional services as a proxy signal (new):** If bundled AI ACV is genuinely driving complex new deployments (new modules, integrations, security), partner-delivered implementation activity should rise — visible indirectly in ServiceNow’s professional services revenue growth rate relative to subscription growth. A decoupling (subscription growth up, professional services growth flat or declining) would be a tension worth investigating.

**Overall Macro/Industry:** Neutral-to-Positive. Enterprise AI spending is broadly favorable. Specific execution risk on the pricing model transition is elevated. Microsoft bundling risk in the sub-enterprise segment is a 3–5 year structural headwind on TAM realization, not an immediate existential threat.

#### **6\. Moat Analysis**

#### **6.1 Intangible Assets**

Strong brand within enterprise IT leadership — CIOs and CTOs default to evaluating ServiceNow for any workflow automation mandate. Two decades of accumulated workflow templates, integrations, and best-practice libraries are genuine non-replicable intangibles. A patent portfolio is meaningful but not the primary defensive layer. RaptorDB (proprietary database engine) and the Now Platform data model are technical differentiators at enterprise scale.

#### **6.2 Switching Costs — The Dominant Moat**

Enterprise customers who have migrated ITSM, ITOM, HR, and CSM onto the Now Platform have embedded it into organizational processes, approval chains, compliance records, and employee behavior patterns. Migration cost is not software licensing — it is accumulated workflow logic, custom configurations, compliance audit trails, and user training investment. This is the moat category that compounds durability most reliably over time.

Each additional module deployed adds a switching cost layer. The $5M+ ACV cohort (603 customers, +20% YoY) represents the most entrenched segment — but the causal variable is module depth, not ACV. A customer running four modules at $2M ACV is more entrenched than a single-module $6M customer. The partner ecosystem further compounds switching costs: the global talent pool trained on ServiceNow (Accenture, Deloitte, KPMG, Wipro) is orders of magnitude larger than any competitor, making ServiceNow the path of least resistance for enterprise IT implementation teams.

#### **6.3 Cost Advantages — Moderate**

Scale economies in cloud infrastructure provide better per-unit compute/storage costs versus smaller competitors. The partner ecosystem network effects represent a genuine structural cost advantage — customers switching away from ServiceNow must simultaneously retrain the entire implementation partner ecosystem, not just their internal teams.

#### **6.4 Overall Moat Assessment**

**Wide** — consistent with Morningstar’s Wide Economic Moat rating. The moat is deep and durable in the multi-module, high-ACV installed base. Moat extension into sub-$1M new logos is increasingly contested by Microsoft’s bundled motion. The 2030 $30B subscription revenue target requires moat extension to succeed — this is the central TAM realization risk.

#### **7\. Valuation Analysis**

#### **7.1 Life Cycle Stage**

ServiceNow is a **Late-Stage Compounder**, not an early-growth optionality play. At $13B+ subscription revenue, growing ~20–21% with 35% FCF margins, this is a demonstrated compounding machine. The appropriate valuation anchors are **cash flow multiples (EV/FCF, P/FCF)**, not EV/NTM Revenue.

#### **7.2 Current Valuation — GAAP-Anchored**

**All multiples in this section are GAAP unless explicitly labeled otherwise.**

- Stock price (May 8, 2026): ~$91.60 (post 5-for-1 split)

- Market cap: ~$94B

- **Post-Armis enterprise value:** ~$99–100B (market cap + ~$5–6B estimated net debt post-$7.75B Armis close, substantially debt-financed)


**TTM GAAP P/E:** Using FY2025 GAAP net income $1,748M + Q1 2026 $469M − Q1 2025 ~$400M = TTM net income ~$1.82B. At $94B market cap → **TTM GAAP P/E ≈ 51–52x**. This is the correct anchor.

**Forward GAAP P/E:** Annualizing Q1 2026 GAAP net income of $469M → ~$1.9B FY2026 GAAP net income → **forward GAAP P/E ≈ 49–50x.** The compression from TTM ~51x to forward ~50x is modest — not the dramatic re-rating that any non-GAAP forward P/E figure would suggest.

⚠️ **Non-GAAP forward P/E figures (21–26x range) appearing in sell-side research strip out ~$2.3B in annual SBC.** These are non-GAAP constructs and are explicitly excluded from this analysis as primary valuation anchors. They may appear as reference points when labeled, but they cannot be compared to the GAAP P/E anchor without reconciliation.

**EV/FCF (TTM, corrected):** Using ~$100B EV and FY2025 FCF of $4.636B (most recent full-year figure) → **EV/FCF ≈ 21.6x**. GuruFocus reported ~19.9x EV/FCF as of April 10, 2026 (pre-Armis close) — the post-Armis net debt adjustment revises this upward modestly. Against the 10-year median EV/FCF of 58.77x, current levels represent a ~63% discount to the historical median.

**Forward EV/FCF (FY2028 base case):** 34.5% FCF margin × $18B FY2028 subscription revenue = **~$6.2B FCF**. At $100B current EV → **EV/FCF of ~16x forward**. A 16x EV/FCF for a wide-moat compounder growing FCF at 17–20%+ is difficult to justify as “fairl valued” under any plausible DCF.

The stock has undergone a severe multiple compression (51.6% market cap decline) while business fundamentals remained broadly intact. This is a textbook fundamental price divergence. The compression reflects macro risk-off, AI model transition uncertainty, and rotation away from legacy SaaS names — not a deterioration in the compounding engine.

#### **7.4 Peer Comparison**

No single peer is a clean comparable for ServiceNow’s horizontal workflow platform category. Salesforce (decelerated growth, lower multiples), SAP (legacy ERP transition, different economics), and Workday (HCM vertical) provide context but not direct comp discipline.

**Morningstar fair value:** ~$975 pre-split (~$195 post-split equivalent), based on $350B TAM by 2027 and $30B subscription revenue by 2030. ⚠️ This is a model-derived DCF, not a market price. Apply as a reference point only.

**Microsoft moat extension risk adjustment to Morningstar target:** A 15–20% compression in TAM realization for the sub-enterprise segment (approximately 25% of incremental revenue path to $30B) would reduce the 2030 target to ~$27.5–28.5B. At 34.5% FCF margin, the NPV impact at a 9% discount rate reduces the implied fair value from ~$195 to approximately **$170–180 post-split**. Still represents ~90% upside from current levels at $91. The investment decision is not materially changed by this adjustment, but the sensitivity should be noted.

#### **7.5 Quantified Reward/Risk**

![](https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!Emg8!,w_1456,c_limit,f_auto,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F1ea8a134-753b-455b-b57c-87c8899625f8_733x121.png)

**Reward/risk ratio: ~2.0–2.3:1 on an EV basis** (24% upside / 11–12% downside). This is the defensible range. Earlier iterations produced 4.5:1 (mixed equity/EV — incorrect) and 2.5:1 (arithmetic error). The corrected 2.2:1 ratio is still comfortably asymmetric for a wide-moat compounder at a partial starter position. It justifies the 30–40% initial allocation.

**Mark-to-market tolerance note:** The 2.2:1 reward/risk ratio is a 2–3 year thesis, not a near-term price target. The stock fell 62% from peak to the April 2026 low while the business continued growing at 20%+ FCF. A further 20–25% drawdown before recovery is plausible — particularly if Q2 2026 misses consensus on constant-currency growth, or if Microsoft makes a high-profile ITSM announcement that reframes the competitive narrative. Position sizing should be calibrated to mark-to-market tolerance, not just thesis quality.

EX-99.1 3 erq1fy26.htm EX-99.1 Document ![servicenow_logo.jpg](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1373715/000137371526000054/servicenow_logo.jpg) ServiceNow Reports First Quarter 2026 Financial Results •ServiceNow beats high end of guidance across all Q1 2026 topline growth and profitability metrics, raises full year subscription revenues outlook •Subscription revenues of $3,671 million in Q1 2026, representing 22% year-over-year growth, 19% in constant currency •Total revenues of $3,770 million in Q1 2026, representing 22% year-over-year growth, 19% in constant currency •Current remaining performance obligations of $12.64 billion as of Q1 2026, representing 22.5% year-over-year growth, 21% in constant currency •Remaining performance obligations of $27.7 billion as of Q1 2026, representing 25% year-over-year growth, 23.5% in constant currency •Now Assist customers spending over $1 million in annual contract value grew over 130% year-over-year SANTA CLARA, Calif. - April 22, 2026 - ServiceNow (NYSE: NOW), the AI control tower for business reinvention, today announced financial results for its first quarter ended March 31, 2026, with subscription revenues of $3,671 million in Q1 2026, representing 22% year-over-year growth and 19% in constant currency. “ServiceNow’s first quarter performance beat the high end of our guidance once again,” said ServiceNow Chairman and CEO Bill McDermott. “Since our founding, we’ve built our platform around the work customers need to accomplish. Today, they rely on ServiceNow to be their AI control tower for business reinvention. Customers trust our platform because we integrate with any model, cloud, interface, data, and system they choose to deploy. As new technologies create both opportunity and risk, our two decades of engineering combined with deep business context enable us to orchestrate and secure the agentic enterprise. With this foundation, our AI growth is far exceeding even our own expectations, reinforcing our position as one of the fastest growing enterprise software companies ever.” As of March 31, 2026, current remaining performance obligations (“cRPO”), contract revenue that will be recognized as revenue in the next 12 months, was $12.64 billion, representing 22.5% year-over-year growth and 21% in constant currency. The company had 16 transactions over $5 million in net new annual contract value (“ACV”) in Q1 2026, representing nearly 80% year-over-year growth, and ended the quarter with 630 customers with more than $5 million in ACV, representing approximately 22% year-over-year growth. “In Q1, we exceeded the high end of our topline and profitability guidance metrics, grew free cash flow, and returned capital to shareholders,” said ServiceNow President and CFO Gina Mastantuono. “The early close of our Armis acquisition meaningfully expands our TAM and accelerates our subscription revenue growth trajectory. With agentic AI, workflow orchestration, security, and data fabric converging on a single platform, we believe the most compelling chapter in ServiceNow's growth story is just beginning.” Recent Business Highlights Innovation This quarter, ServiceNow advanced enterprise AI into new product categories, new ways of working, and a new commercial model. | | | | | | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | | | | | | | | 2 | ![pro013945_stylesheetxlogo.jpg](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1373715/000137371526000054/pro013945_stylesheetxlogo.jpg) | * * * •In April, ServiceNow delivered a complete AI-native experience across every commercial tier, with AI, data connectivity, workflow execution, security, and governance built in by default. At the center is Context Engine, the organizational intelligence that grounds every AI decision in live enterprise context: which asset ties to a regulated process, which approval chain applies, and which decision precedent governs the outcome. New Build Agent Skills let developers build from any tool they already use and deploy directly to ServiceNow. •ServiceNow also launched Autonomous Workforce, a new class of AI specialists that execute enterprise jobs end-to-end with built-in governance and human oversight. The first available out-of-the-box is a Level 1 Service Desk AI Specialist that autonomously diagnoses and resolves common IT support requests. •ServiceNow announced ServiceNow EmployeeWorks, a conversational front door for the enterprise that connects intent to governed action across any system, combining Moveworks' AI and enterprise search with ServiceNow's autonomous workflows to turn plain-language requests into completed actions. Partnerships ServiceNow's partner ecosystem expanded significantly in Q1, with leading companies building on the platform to deliver AI at a global scale. •ServiceNow and Google Cloud unveiled a suite of AI solutions spanning 5G networks, retail, and IT operations, enabling enterprises to detect and resolve issues before they reach customers. Google Cloud also named ServiceNow its 2026 Partner of the Year for Global Business Applications and Agentic Innovation. •ServiceNow and NVIDIA advanced their partnership in building governed enterprise AI at NVIDIA GTC in March, announcing how ServiceNow Autonomous Workforce can leverage NVIDIA’s latest AI infrastructure. The companies also previewed a new integration between the NVIDIA Enterprise AI Factory and ServiceNow AI Control Tower, along with a joint benchmarking framework for voice and multimodal AI deployment. •ServiceNow, NTT DOCOMO, and StarHub introduced the industry's first inter-carrier autonomous roaming resolution model using ServiceNow CRM to automatically detect, diagnose, and resolve faults across carrier boundaries in real time. Industry Expansion This quarter, the ServiceNow AI Platform drove measurable outcomes across multiple industries, turning industry depth into operational results. •TridentCare deployed the ServiceNow AI Platform to transform end-to-end operations across 5.4 million annual patient visits, replacing manual coordination with autonomous, AI-driven processes and achieving 96% scheduling automation and a 57% reduction in patient wait times. •ServiceNow debuted Healthcare Operations, a new solution that embeds a shared operational system of record directly into the electronic medical record system to connect care teams with facilities, biomed, and IT support on a single platform, giving clinicians more time for patient care. •Bell, Canada's leading telecommunications provider, reported a 25% improvement in customer response time and 90% positive feedback on AI accuracy after deploying ServiceNow AI Agents in Telecom, powered by ServiceNow Autonomous CRM. •ServiceNow unveiled Industrial Connected Workforce, allowing fragmented quality, warranty, orders, and quoting systems to be connected in a single operational view and replacing paper-based processes with real-time digital guidance to preserve institutional knowledge as experienced workers retire. Acquisitions ServiceNow closed two acquisitions that are designed to give enterprises a unified, end-to-end security stack that can see, decide, and act across the entire technology footprint. •ServiceNow closed its acquisition of Armis on April 20, 2026. By combining Armis' real-time asset discovery and cyber exposure management with ServiceNow's AI Control Tower and automated workflows, the two companies intend to deliver a unified, end-to-end security platform that can see, decide, and act across environments. | | | | | | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | | | | | | | | ![pro013945_stylesheetxlogo.jpg](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1373715/000137371526000054/pro013945_stylesheetxlogo.jpg) | 3 | * * * •ServiceNow closed its acquisition of Veza on March 2, 2026. The acquisition extends ServiceNow’s security capabilities and aims to give enterprises complete visibility and control over who and what can access critical data, applications, and AI agents. Investment •ServiceNow repurchased approximately 20.1 million shares of common stock during Q1, with the primary objective of managing the impact of dilution, including 18.5 million shares through its previously announced $2B accelerated share repurchase as well as another 1.6 million shares for $225 million through open market transactions. As of the end of the quarter, approximately $4.2 billion remained available under the share repurchase program1. Recognition ServiceNow's leadership in AI innovation and workplace culture earned recognition from analysts and institutions across the industry. •ServiceNow was recognized as a leader in multiple analyst reports, including The Forrester WaveTM: Industry Cloud Solutions for Public Sector, Q1 20262, The Forrester WaveTM: Customer Service Solutions, Q1 20263, the IDC MarketScape: Worldwide AIOps 2026 Vendor Assessment4, the 2026 ISG Buyers Guide™ for Application Platforms5, and the 2026 ISG Buyers Guide™ for Field Service Management6. •ServiceNow was named to Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies 2026 list in Applied AI and Ethisphere’s 2026 World’s Most Ethical Companies, reflecting the company’s commitment to responsible, cutting-edge AI innovation. ServiceNow also earned a spot on Glassdoor’s Best Places to Work in Tech and AI 2026 list and the inaugural American Opportunity Index’s Where You Work Matters list, highlighting employers that invest in workforce growth and opportunity. (1)The program does not have a fixed expiration date, may be suspended, or discontinued at any time, and does not obligate ServiceNow to acquire any amount of its common stock. The timing, manner, price, and amount of any repurchases will be determined by ServiceNow at its discretion and will depend on a variety of factors, including business, economic and market conditions, prevailing stock prices, corporate and regulatory requirements, and other considerations. The non‑GAAP growth rates for subscription revenues are adjusted for constant currency by excluding the effects of foreign currency rate fluctuations and any gains or losses from foreign currency hedge contracts, and the non-GAAP growth rates for cRPO are adjusted only for constant currency to provide better visibility into the underlying business. In Q1 2026, subscription revenues growth saw an approximately 75 basis point headwind from delayed closings of several large on-premise deals in the Middle East, due to the ongoing conflict in the region. This outlook reflects a prudent assessment of those geopolitical headwinds on deal timing for the remainder of FY 2026. Our Q2 2026 subscription revenues growth, Q2 2026 cRPO growth, and FY 2026 subscription revenues growth guidance each include approximately 125 basis points of contribution from Armis. A portion of Armis customer contracts include termination‑for‑convenience provisions, which limit the amount of contract value reflected in cRPO. The acquisition is also expected to create headwinds of approximately 25 basis points to FY 2026 subscription gross margin, approximately 75 basis points to FY 2026 operating margin, approximately 200 basis points to FY 2026 free cash flow margin, and approximately 125 basis points to Q2 2026 operating margin. While we will see some near-term headwinds to margins as we integrate the business in FY 2026, strong AI efficiencies internally from Now on Now and our underlying platform leverage are expected to normalize our operating and free cash flow margin expansion trajectories in FY 2027. Statement Regarding Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures We use the following non-GAAP financial measures in addition to, and not as a substitute for, or superior to, financial measures calculated in accordance with GAAP. •Revenues. We adjust revenues and related growth rates for constant currency to provide a framework for assessing how our business performed excluding the effect of foreign currency rate fluctuations and any gains or losses from foreign currency hedge contracts that are reported in the current and comparative period. To exclude the effect of foreign currency rate fluctuations, current period results for entities reporting in currencies other than U.S. Dollars (“USD”) are converted into USD at the average exchange rates in effect during the comparison period (for Q1 2025, the average exchange rates in effect for our major currencies were | | | | | | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | | | | | | | | 8 | ![pro013945_stylesheetxlogo.jpg](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1373715/000137371526000054/pro013945_stylesheetxlogo.jpg) | * * * 1 USD to 0.95 Euros and 1 USD to 0.79 British Pound Sterling (“GBP”)), rather than the actual average exchange rates in effect during the current period (for Q1 2026, the average exchange rates in effect for our major currencies were 1 USD to 0.85 Euros and 1 USD to 0.74 GBP). Guidance for revenues related growth rates is derived by applying the average exchange rates in effect during the comparison period, rather than the exchange rates for the guidance period, adjusted for any foreign currency hedging effects. We believe the presentation of revenues and related growth rates adjusted for constant currency facilitates the comparison of revenues year-over-year. •Remaining performance obligations and current remaining performance obligations. We adjust cRPO and remaining performance obligations (“RPO”) and related growth rates for constant currency to provide a framework for assessing how our business performed. To present this information, current period results for entities reporting in currencies other than USD are converted into USD at the exchange rates in effect at the end of the comparison period (for Q1 2025, the end of the period exchange rates in effect for our major currencies were 1 USD to 0.92 Euros and 1 USD to 0.77 GBP), rather than the actual end of the period exchange rates in effect during the current period (for Q1 2026, the end of the period exchange rates in effect for our major currencies were 1 USD to 0.87 Euros and 1 USD to 0.76 GBP). Guidance for the related growth rate is derived by applying the end of period exchange rates in effect during the comparison period rather than the exchange rates in effect during the guidance period. We believe the presentation of cRPO and RPO and related growth rates adjusted for constant currency facilitates the comparison of cRPO and RPO year-over-year, respectively. •Gross profit, Income from operations, Net income and Net income per share - diluted. Our non-GAAP presentation of gross profit, income from operations, and net income measures exclude certain non-cash or non-recurring items, including stock-based compensation expense, amortization of purchased intangibles, legal settlements, impairment of assets, severance costs, contract termination costs, business combination and other related costs including compensation expense, gains and losses on strategic investments, net, and income tax effects and adjustments. We believe these adjustments provide useful supplemental information to investors and facilitates the analysis of our operating results and comparison of operating results across reporting periods. •Free cash flow. Free cash flow is defined as net cash provided by operating activities plus cash outflows for legal settlements and business combination and other related costs including compensation expense, reduced by purchases of property and equipment. Free cash flow margin is calculated as free cash flow as a percentage of total revenues. We believe information regarding free cash flow and free cash flow margin provides useful information to investors because it is an indicator of the strength and performance of our business operations. Our presentation of non-GAAP financial measures may not be comparable to similar measures used by other companies. We encourage investors to carefully consider our results under GAAP, as well as our supplemental non-GAAP information and the reconciliation between these presentations, to more fully understand our business. criteria.earnings_release: A company earnings announcement with reported financial results.
criteria.investor_presentation: The actual investor presentation or slide contents, not an event listing.
criteria.technical_documentation: Operational API/reference documentation with endpoints, parameters, or implementation instructions.
criteria.product_description: A product or app listing, marketing page, or descriptive product data sheet, including a product that manages contracts.
criteria.commercial_agreement: The substantive subscription/service agreement itself with contractual rights and obligations, regardless of its age or hosting authority.
criteria.external_analysis: An external commentator's analysis of the business or investment thesis, even if generated, bullish, inaccurate, or unverified.
criteria.news_report: A news report summarizing another party's announcement or research, rather than that original research.
criteria.event_announcement: An announcement of a forthcoming or past event, not the presentation contents.
criteria.index_navigation: An index or navigation/listing page linking to documents instead of containing the expected document.
criteria.ownership_filing: A filing about insider ownership or ownership changes.
criteria.unknown: Insufficient supplied content or none of the listed document types.

# HR REST API

Release version: Brazil

Updated September 10, 2026

![](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/portal-asset/ico-clock) 4 minutes to read

The HR REST API provides endpoints that return information about
employees that work or live in the United States.

To access this API you must have the sn\_hr\_core.usa\_employee\_only role and the Human
Resources Scoped App: Core (com\_sn\_hr\_core) plugin activated.

## HR REST - GET /get\_usa\_employee\_profile

Returns employee profile information for employees based in the United
States.

The returned information can be either:

- Employee profile information for a specified employee ID.
- Information for employees that have been added, or whose information has been updated, on or after a specified date.

Note:

Employees must either have their work or home country specified as the United States for this endpoint to include them in the return results.

In addition, the endpoint sends the following parameters to the integrated CIC Plus
application (see the Returns section for descriptions):

- EmployeeIdentifier
- FirstName
- MiddleName
- LastName
- Email
- WorkAddress
- WorkCity
- WorkState
- WorkPostalCode
- WorkCountry
- HomeAddress
- HomeCity
- HomeState
- HomePostalCode
- HomeCountry
- BirthDate
- HireDate

### URL format

Default URL:
/api/sn\_hr\_core/hr\_rest\_api/get\_usa\_employee\_profile

### Supported request parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| None |  |

Table 1. Path parameters

| Parameter | Description |
| --- | --- |
| employee\_identifier | Unique identifier of an employee. The calling system generates this value and can be in whatever format is consistent with their system. To obtain this value, first call the endpoint using the<br> updated\_after parameter.<br>Note:<br>This parameter is mutually exclusive with the updated\_after parameter. This parameter defines a unique employee, whereas<br>updated\_after returns a group of employees created/updated after a specified date.<br>Data type: String |
| sysparm\_limit | Maximum number of records to return. For requests that exceed this number of records, use the sysparm\_offset parameter to paginate record retrieval.<br>Data type: Number<br>Default: 1000 |
| sysparm\_offset | Starting record index for which to begin retrieving records. Use this value to paginate record retrieval. This functionality enables the retrieval of all records, regardless of the<br> number of records, in small manageable chunks.<br>For example, the first time you call this endpoint, sysparm\_offset is set to "0". To simply page through all available records, use<br>`sysparm_offset=sysparm_offset+sysparm_limit`, until you reach the end of all records. |
| updated\_after | Date to use to determine the employee data to return. All United States-based employees (work or home) that were added to your instance, or whose information was updated on or after this date, are included in the<br> return results.<br>Note:<br>This parameter is mutually exclusive with the employee\_identifier parameter.<br>Data type: String<br>Format: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS or YYYY-MM-DD (time defaults to<br>00:00:00) |

Table 2. Query parameters

| Name | Description |
| --- | --- |
| None |  |

Table 3. Request body parameters (XML or JSON)

### Headers

The following request and response headers apply to this HTTP
action only, or apply to this action in a distinct way. For a list of general headers used
in the REST API, see [Supported REST API headers](https://www.servicenow.com/docs/r/ooCZhg2g6YDYvKp3oBwAxA/TSHwMH5MZNTdV2wXSUhSiw "REST (REpresentational State Transfer) is a simple stateless architecture that provides standards between computer systems on the web, making it easier for them to communicate with each other.").

| Header | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Accept | Data format of the response body. Supported types: application/json or application/xml.<br>Default: application/json |

Table 4. Request headers

| Header | Description |
| --- | --- |
| Next-Page | Flag that indicates whether there is additional data to obtain in a subsequent<br> call. For example, if there are a total of 120 employee records that match the<br> search criteria, and sysparm\_limit is set to 100, then<br> Next-Page is true. If no additional results are available,<br> Next-Page is false.<br>Valid values:<br>- true: Additional data is available, another call must be made to obtain the<br>next chunk of data.<br>- false: No additional data. |

| 401 | Unauthorized. The user credentials are incorrect or<br> have not been passed. |
| 404 | Not found. The requested item wasn't found. |
| 500 | Internal server error. An unexpected error occurred<br> while processing the request. The response contains additional information about the<br> error. |

| WorkState | Employee's work state.<br>Data type: String |

passages.p000: Using the DCF framework from our ServiceNow DCFriday valuation work, the numbers become far more interesting than the headline multiples suggest. Our model starts with FY2025 revenue of $13.28B and assumes revenue growth of 20.5% in 2026, gradually fading to 4.5% by 2035. The base case uses an 8.5% WACC, a 2.5% terminal growth rate, and GAAP EBIT margin expansion from 15% toward 22.5% over projected time. On these assumptions, intrinsic value comes out around $160 per share. The bear case lands us at about $98.5, while the bull case reaches roughly $199.
passages.p001: As far as competition goes, the peer set is broad, but not all competitors threaten ServiceNow equally. Microsoft, Oracle, SAP, Salesforce, and Workday all compete in parts of the market, yet their products are often systems of record rather than cross-enterprise workflow layers. ServiceNow has historically complemented those suites by orchestrating work across them instead of replacing them. The risk here is that large vendors keep adding workflow and AI features to their own platforms, reducing the need for an independent orchestration layer. That matters even more in an AI world, where every vendor wants to be the “agentic” layer for enterprise automation, especially since it’s such a buzzword these days.
passages.p002: The company’s 10‑K states AI systems may not perform as intended and may generate unreliable or biased results, potentially harming customer trust and creating liability. It also flags heightened IP / copyright infringement and other legal challenges associated with AI. Positive here is that the company is quite honest about AI in its 10-K. However, because ServiceNow’s strategy increasingly positions AI agents as executors of workflow actions (thus “agents”, not just “answers”), model failures can translate into real operational errors (access grants, ticket closures, workflow triggers,…), increasing the tail risk of customer losses or regulated-client disputes.
passages.p006: ServiceNow’s software model delivers strong gross margins and improving operating margins. In FY2025, subscription gross margin was about 80% GAAP ($10,314M of $12,883M subscription revenue). On a non-GAAP basis (ex-stock comp/amortisation), subscription gross margin was 83.5%, down slightly from 85% in 2024. The dip reflects upfront costs for new AI services and acquired products (e.g. Moveworks). Management projects modest gross-margin compression (guidance of 82% in 2026) as newer offerings scale. Nonetheless, the ballpark of 80%-85% gross margin is very healthy, reflecting high software leverage.

passages.p003:
ServiceNow also sits
across fragmented technology stacks. Large enterprises run multiple systems
such as Salesforce, SAP, Oracle, Snowflake and Databricks, alongside different
model providers such as OpenAI, Anthropic and Google. ServiceNow acts as the
workflow layer connecting them, allowing data and AI outputs to flow across
applications while governance, permissions and audit controls are maintained.
This model-agnostic approach lets enterprises adopt different models and data
sources without locking into one ecosystem.
passages.p004:
Instead of open-ended
token billing, ServiceNow embedded hybrid pricing across tiers, giving
customers broader AI access while monetising incremental usage through
entitlements, service credits and Assist Packs. Pricing remains primarily
subscription-based, charged per fulfiller user (employees who actively manage
or resolve workflows). Pricing varies by product and tier, but industry
benchmarks suggest ITSM pricing can range from roughly USD 90 to USD 200+ per
user per month, with higher tiers such as Pro Plus or Enterprise Plus costing
more for added analytics, automation and generative AI.
passages.p005:
Higher AI inference costs could pressure
subscription gross margins if customer adoption accelerates faster than
ServiceNow's ability to monetise AI usage through hybrid pricing. While
management currently expects subscription gross margins above 80%, sustained
increases in compute intensity remain a key execution risk.
passages.p006:
ServiceNow deserves a
premium multiple due to its sticky workflow base, 98% renewal rate, strong FCF
margin, durable 20%+ subscription growth and early AI monetisation through Now
Assist, whose ACV already exceeds USD 750Mn against an FY2026 target of USD
1.5Bn. With that, we value ServiceNow on FY2028E EPS of
USD 6.08 at a fair P/E of 24x, implying a target price of USD144.70 and 38%
upside from USD 104.85.

passages.p003: The customer profile is systematically upper-enterprise. Sub-enterprise deployment is a structural gap in go-to-market, and the primary arena where Microsoft’s bundled competitive motion is most dangerous (see Sections 4.3 and 5.4).
passages.p004: In core ITSM, ServiceNow holds near-oligopoly status. The distant second tier — BMC Helix, Atlassian Jira Service Management — does not threaten the installed base. The genuine rivalry is in expansion adjacencies: CRM (Salesforce), HR workflows (Workday, SAP), and security operations (Palo Alto, CrowdStrike). In these adjacencies, ServiceNow is the challenger, not the incumbent, and the single-platform consolidation argument, while real, is harder to prove in greenfield deals where the incumbent is deeply embedded.
passages.p005: The generic AI agent substitute threat (Microsoft Copilot, Google Gemini) is real, but generic framing understates the specific mechanism. Microsoft’s threat is not that Copilot is technically superior to ServiceNow’s ITSM workflow engine — it almost certainly is not for complex multi-workflow scenarios. The threat is that Microsoft can offer **“good enough bundled”** IT workflow automation as part of Microsoft 365 / Azure agreements that enterprises already pay for. This is the most historically dangerous competitive motion against best-of-breed SaaS.
passages.p006: Scale economies in cloud infrastructure provide better per-unit compute/storage costs versus smaller competitors. The partner ecosystem network effects represent a genuine structural cost advantage — customers switching away from ServiceNow must simultaneously retrain the entire implementation partner ecosystem, not just their internal teams.

passages.p001: _ServiceNow makes the world work better for everyone.
